text: ds-harness-remote 是面向 DSH 浏览器和桌面 Host 的远程访问插件，可让 Web 与 Android 等客户端连接本机工作区。它将插件注入 DSH 连接、侧边栏和设置界面，并通过对等连接支持 Harness 会话、文件浏览与传输、终端及可选的 Codex/ACP 工作区。内置 Remote Tools 可发现主机和工作区、读写 Harness 会话并等待执行状态。适合需要离开电脑后继续处理本地项目的用户；需要 Remote 账户和可用的 Remote Server。

ds-harness-remote connects web and Android clients to a DSH desktop Host. It exposes Harness sessions, workspace files and terminals. Optional Codex and ACP backends extend workspace access. Remote Tools discover Hosts and manage sessions. A Remote account and reachable server are required.
想从手机接着使用电脑上打开的 DSH 工作区。
我出门后怎么继续查看家里电脑上的 Harness 会话？
需要在浏览器里连接本地 DSH 项目并继续工作。
能不能远程列出主机上的工作区和已有会话？
让 DSH 会话能从远端上传或下载工作区文件。
我想在另一台设备上查看远程会话的历史和运行状态。
I want to continue a local DSH workspace from my phone while away from my computer.
How can I browse my remote Host workspaces and inspect a Harness session from a browser?
I need to transfer a project file to a remote Harness session workspace.
Can I open a terminal on the computer running my remote workspace?
ds-harness-remote 的功能「Remote Tools」：向本地 Harness 会话提供远端主机与工作区发现工具，并注册会话操作工具。
ds-harness-remote 的功能「远程会话」：可创建 Harness 会话、发送消息、读取历史并查询执行状态。
ds-harness-remote 的功能「文件传输」：在用户指定的本地文件与远程 Harness 工作区间上传或下载文件。
ds-harness-remote 的功能「远程终端」：通过 Host 提供的 subprocess 服务为连接的客户端建立终端会话。
ds-harness-remote 的功能「移动端连接」：Android 客户端可登录 Remote 服务、查看主机并连接到工作区。
ds-harness-remote 的功能「远程连接」：Host 与客户端协商 WebRTC 或 Relay 传输，并在通道上使用加密消息协议。
ds-harness-remote 使用的默认 Remote Server 为 dsh.r2049.cn；账户与连接需要访问配置的服务端，部署也可设置其他 serverUrl。

ds-harness-remote README · Connect once. Ready whenever you are.：Continue using your DeepSeek Harness instance from a phone, computer, or browser. Return to the same Harness session from whichever device is with you.

Harness keeps running on your work computer, with the same workspaces, tools, and project setup. DS Harness Remote is simply another window into that environment.

The DeepSeek Harness desktop edition is supported. Install the latest release:

`ds-harness-remote@0.6.3`

ds-harness-remote README · Features：- Access your local Harness instance remotely from the web, a PC, or a mobile device: DSH first, with Codex, Cursor, and Antigravity support too.
- DeepSeek Harness Desktop is ready to use after installation, with its native interface and no separate desktop conversation UI.
- Create workspaces, configure models, and switch conversation models with the same smooth workflow as local use.
- No public listening port or public IP is required on the Harness Host. Connect from anywhere with internet access over a bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel.
- Prefer P2P connections, use TURN relay nodes worldwide, and fall back to multiple Server Relays when needed.
- Access workspace files, read-only previews, remote terminals, and authorized local development-service previews through the native Harness sidebar.

ds-harness-remote README · Supported clients：Several clients can connect to the same Host at once; RPC calls and streams are isolated per connection.

ds-harness-remote README · DeepSeek Harness Desktop support：Open **Extensions / Plugin management** in DeepSeek Harness Desktop, choose installation
from npm, and enter this package:

`ds-harness-remote@0.6.3`

Restart Desktop afterward. Its official `dsh` launcher can also install the pinned package
with `dsh plugin --profile desktop add -w ds-harness-remote@0.6.3`.

ds-harness-remote README · DeepSeek Harness Desktop support：On DSH 0.2.2+, npm installations support version checks and updates in Plugin management, with an attempt to restore the previous version if hot updating fails. GitHub and local link installations must switch to npm first; see [online updates](docs/installation.md#online-updates-in-dsh-plugin-management).
ds-harness-remote README · Linux one-command installation：Visit [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn/), sign in, and obtain an installation authorization code to install with one command.

ds-harness-remote README · Native Android client：Keep conversations connected across multiple workspaces at once, and use **Bot mode**, powered by [Fei2411/DS-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot).

Download the latest APK from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/releases/latest), and sign in to the same account to see your Hosts.

ds-harness-remote README · DSH Go — DeepSeek Harness in your pocket: run it locally on your phone or control your computer remotely.：[ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go) has built-in support for the ds-harness-remote protocol. You can run DeepSeek Harness locally on your phone or connect to your computer remotely.

After installing the ds-harness-remote plugin in DSH Go on your phone, you can also connect to the phone’s DSH from your computer or the web and use Mobile Use seamlessly.

ds-harness-remote README · Quick start：1. Open **Remote** from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar.
2. Choose Zhihu, GitHub, or Google authorization, or sign in with an account and password. Account registration requires an invitation code; email the repository author to request one.
3. On another device, install the same plugin in DeepSeek Harness and sign in as described in steps 1–2. Alternatively, use Remote Web, iOS, Android, or DSH Go directly without installing a plugin.
4. Select an online Host, then choose an existing workspace or browse remote directories to open one.

ds-harness-remote README · Quick start：By default, Remote uses this project's hosted Server at [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn).

For self-hosting, use the repository's [minimal Server](apps/server/README.md). The current version includes WebRTC LAN/P2P/TURN coordination (TURN requires your own coturn deployment) and an encrypted Relay Server, but does not provide the full hosted Remote Web experience.

ds-harness-remote README · Desktop：On another computer, select an online Host and open its workspace. The workspace opens in the native Harness interface, with the active Host and encrypted connection status in the header.

ds-harness-remote README · Desktop：To prevent this computer from controlling other Hosts, open the Host list at [https://dsh.r2049.cn/](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) and enable **Controlled only**. This device will no longer see other devices under your account, while Web and other clients can still connect to it remotely.

ds-harness-remote README · Android：Use text or image prompts, switch models, and access supported workspace files and terminals.

The interface follows the system language and supports English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, German, and French. In language settings, tap “More ...” to show all languages. See the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) for details.

ds-harness-remote README · Android：

Mobile Settings includes a global **Compact conversations** switch, off by default and applied when a conversation is next opened.
ds-harness-remote README · Android：Supporting Hosts reduce historical tool details while preserving messages and tool status. Turn the setting off and reopen the conversation to load full history.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：```text
DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android
  ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel
Remote Plugin on the Host
  ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support

The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. Connect from anywhere with internet access over ds-harness-remote’s bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel.

The client switches to the selected Host’s native Harness API, keeping the original workspaces, tools, and permission flows on that computer.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：You can also edit Harness and plugin settings on the remote host. Available options depend on which settings Harness and each plugin expose through the official settings API.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：The Host runs local ACP-capable Agents and forwards prompts, streamed replies, and approvals through ds-harness-remote. Each Agent keeps its own workspaces and sessions; only session translation for DSH is performed, without writing to Harness storage.

Supported backends:

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：- **Codex** — connects through App Server, using the shared workspace entry.
- **Cursor** — connects through the CLI's ACP interface.
- **Antigravity (AGY)** — connects through an adapter for its stream-json CLI.
- **Pi Agent (experimental)** — automatically detected after installing and configuring Pi and `pi-acp`; can be disabled in settings. Tools run with Host-user permissions, without per-tool confirmation by default.
- **OpenCode** — connects through `opencode acp`, with workspaces and history. Session archiving requires a build with the authenticated API; unarchive is not yet available.
- **Claude** — connects through a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text and approvals; images are not yet supported.
- **Hermes** — connects through `hermes acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text, images, streamed output, approvals, and model selection.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：Claude and Hermes also support direct file and terminal access, subject to the Host's workspace boundaries and terminal settings.

Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md).

Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog as determined by the Agent’s ACP interface.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：Reasoning effort options depend on what the backend provides. Cursor uses a separate process per session, so model changes do not affect other conversations.

ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：Harness business traffic is encrypted on the Client and decrypted only by the selected Host using the fixed `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` suite.

Connections must pass both same-account membership and locally pinned device identity key checks.

The service can coordinate connections and observe necessary network metadata, but it cannot read session messages, prompts, tool output, workspace paths, or remote file contents.
ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：See [End-to-end encryption](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md) for the handshake, key lifecycle, visible metadata, replay protection, and security limits.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：The Host opens outbound connections only; it does not listen on a public port or require router port forwarding.

Remote negotiates paths in the order `LAN -> P2P -> TURN -> Relay`.

When WebRTC is unavailable or cannot connect, it falls back to the encrypted WebSocket Relay.

Every path carries the same Noise ciphertext and keeps the same Host/Client identity boundary.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：See [Network and transport](docs/network.md) for the topology, control and data planes, NAT behavior, fallback, reconnect semantics, and current validation status.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- On LAN and P2P paths, data bypasses the Server except for connection coordination. TURN uses the open-source coturn server; Relay mode forwards traffic over WebSocket.
- Session traffic is end-to-end encrypted. The service relays ciphertext without storing session plaintext or device private keys.
- Same-account devices connect without extra confirmation; see [device trust and permissions](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md#2-设备身份与信任).
- [Remote Tools injection](docs/remote-tools.md) — optional `remote_*` session tools; enabled by default and configurable in detailed Remote settings.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- Interactive terminals use the Host-local `terminal.enabled` switch (on by default). They run as the Host user, independently of Agent approvals.
- General tool RPC and remote desktop are not exposed.
- The workspace picker lists folders only and returns bounded, read-only directory metadata.
- Remote file preview cannot write, delete, upload, execute, or open a path in an external application.
- Codex Remote / Agent ACP is optional, can be disabled, and follows the same encrypted Host permission boundary as the rest of Remote.
- Removing a device revokes its credentials, membership, and active Remote connections.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Do I need a public IP or port forwarding?**

No. The Host only opens outbound connections and never listens on a public port.

**Can the service read my conversations?**

No. The service relays ciphertext only. Routing, authorization, presence and rate limiting require control metadata such as account and device ownership, online status, connection times and `connectionId`; prompts, conversation content, tool input and output, workspace paths and file preview contents stay unreadable.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Which machine can act as a Host?**

Any signed-in Harness instance with the Remote plugin installed can act as a Host, whether on Windows, macOS, Linux, or even DSH Go.

**Can several devices connect to one Host at the same time?**

There is currently no limit on concurrent client connections, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection.

**Which Harness versions are supported?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：The current baseline is `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1`; `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5` and `0.2.0` rc.2 / rc.1 remain compatible on the same official carrier. See the [compatibility guide](docs/compatibility.md).

Harness `0.1.1-rc.2` ApiProxy support has been removed from the Host plugin, its bundled Remote client, and Android. Use a Host with the official Typert Remote carrier; Hosts that only provide ApiProxy or lack capability discovery are rejected, with no fallback.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：CodeX/ACP keep their independent data planes, and Desktop projections use Typert in memory.

**Why does the Linux installer require root?**

It configures a systemd system service, so the Host, Agent tools and remote terminals run with root privileges. Only expose it to trusted accounts.

**Can I install the iOS app directly?**

It is in TestFlight beta today and not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20).

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**How is this different from frp, a tunnel, or remote desktop?**

Conventional server-based TCP port forwarding routes traffic through a Server, making its bandwidth a potential bottleneck.

This project probes four connection modes in sequence to establish P2P connections even in complex network environments.

Remote desktop captures the entire computer screen and reproduces it on the client, placing demands on upload and download bandwidth as well as computer performance.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：This project encrypts and transmits only the messages needed by the native Harness conversation interface. General tool RPC and desktop control are not exposed, and permissions and approvals remain on the Host.

Tailscale, CF Turn, and UU Remote are also excellent solutions; choose whichever fits your needs.

ds-harness-remote README · Intelligent UI：[Intelligent UI](https://github.com/dreamfarer-space/deepseek-harness-intelligent-ui) lets models answer with cards, tables, charts, and forms. The Android client renders them natively and lists the plugin under **Plugins → Remote ready**, where you can enable or disable it and edit live settings.

ds-harness-remote README · Quick start：1. Open **Remote** from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar.
2. Choose Zhihu, GitHub, or Google authorization, or sign in with an account and password. Account registration requires an invitation code; email the repository author to request one.
3. On another device, install the same plugin in DeepSeek Harness and sign in as described in steps 1–2. Alternatively, use Remote Web, iOS, Android, or DSH Go directly without installing a plugin.
4. Select an online Host, then choose an existing workspace or browse remote directories to open one.

ds-harness-remote README · Quick start：By default, Remote uses this project's hosted Server at [https://dsh.r2049.cn](https://dsh.r2049.cn).

For self-hosting, use the repository's [minimal Server](apps/server/README.md). The current version includes P2P coordination and a Relay Server, but does not provide the full hosted Remote Web experience.

ds-harness-remote README · Desktop：On another computer, select an online Host and open its workspace. The workspace opens in the native Harness interface, with the active Host and encrypted connection status in the header.

ds-harness-remote README · Desktop：To prevent this computer from controlling other Hosts, open the Host list at [https://dsh.r2049.cn/](https://dsh.r2049.cn/) and enable **Controlled only**. This device will no longer see other devices under your account, while Web and other clients can still connect to it remotely.

ds-harness-remote README · Android：Use text or image prompts, switch models, and access supported workspace files and terminals.

The interface follows the system language and supports English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Spanish, German, and French. In language settings, tap “More ...” to show all languages. See the [Android guide](apps/android/README.md) for details.

ds-harness-remote README · Android：

Mobile Settings includes a global **Compact conversations** switch, off by default and applied when a conversation is next opened.
ds-harness-remote README · Android：Supporting Hosts reduce historical tool details while preserving messages and tool status. Turn the setting off and reopen the conversation to load full history.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：```text
DSH Desktop / Remote Web / Android
  ↔ authenticated, end-to-end encrypted channel
Remote Plugin on the Host
  ↔ supported Harness or optional Codex workspace support

The Harness Host does not need a public listening port. Connect from anywhere with internet access over ds-harness-remote’s bidirectional end-to-end encrypted channel.

The client switches to the selected Host’s native Harness API, keeping the original workspaces, tools, and permission flows on that computer.

ds-harness-remote README · How it works：You can also edit Harness and plugin settings on the remote host. Available options depend on which settings Harness and each plugin expose through the official settings API.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：The Host runs local ACP-capable Agents and forwards prompts, streamed replies, and approvals through ds-harness-remote. Each Agent keeps its own workspaces and sessions; only session translation for DSH is performed, without writing to Harness storage.

Supported backends:

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：- **Codex** — connects through App Server, using the shared workspace entry.
- **Cursor** — connects through the CLI's ACP interface.
- **Antigravity (AGY)** — connects through an adapter for its stream-json CLI.
- **Pi Agent (experimental)** — automatically detected after installing and configuring Pi and `pi-acp`; can be disabled in settings. Tools run with Host-user permissions, without per-tool confirmation by default.
- **OpenCode** — connects through `opencode acp`, with workspaces and history. Session archiving requires a build with the authenticated API; unarchive is not yet available.
- **Claude** — connects through a locally authorized `claude-agent-acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text and approvals; images are not yet supported.
- **Hermes** — connects through `hermes acp`; enable it in settings. Supports text, images, streamed output, approvals, and model selection.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：Claude and Hermes also support direct file and terminal access, subject to the Host's workspace boundaries and terminal settings.

Setup and adapter development: [Agent workspace integration guide](docs/acp-integration.md).

Model selection for Cursor, Claude, Hermes, Pi, OpenCode, and AGY on Desktop/Android uses the Host's actual model catalog as determined by the Agent’s ACP interface.

ds-harness-remote README · Experimental ACP workspaces：Reasoning effort options depend on what the backend provides. Cursor uses a separate process per session, so model changes do not affect other conversations.

ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：Harness business traffic is encrypted on the Client and decrypted only by the selected Host using the fixed `Noise_IK_25519_ChaChaPoly_SHA256` suite.

Connections must pass both same-account membership and locally pinned device identity key checks.

The service can coordinate connections and observe necessary network metadata, but it cannot read session messages, prompts, tool output, workspace paths, or remote file contents.
ds-harness-remote README · End-to-end encryption：See [End-to-end encryption](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md) for the handshake, key lifecycle, visible metadata, replay protection, and security limits.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：The Host opens outbound connections only; it does not listen on a public port or require router port forwarding.

Remote negotiates paths in the order `LAN -> P2P -> TURN -> Relay`.

When WebRTC is unavailable or cannot connect, it falls back to the encrypted WebSocket Relay.

Every path carries the same Noise ciphertext and keeps the same Host/Client identity boundary.

ds-harness-remote README · Network and transport：See [Network and transport](docs/network.md) for the topology, control and data planes, NAT behavior, fallback, reconnect semantics, and current validation status.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- On LAN and P2P paths, data bypasses the Server except for connection coordination. TURN uses the open-source coturn server; Relay mode forwards traffic over WebSocket.
- Session traffic is end-to-end encrypted. The service relays ciphertext without storing session plaintext or device private keys.
- Same-account devices connect without extra confirmation; see [device trust and permissions](docs/end-to-end-encryption.md#2-设备身份与信任).
- [Remote Tools injection](docs/remote-tools.md) — optional `remote_*` session tools; enabled by default and configurable in detailed Remote settings.

ds-harness-remote README · Security：- Interactive terminals use the Host-local `terminal.enabled` switch (on by default). They run as the Host user, independently of Agent approvals.
- General tool RPC and remote desktop are not exposed.
- The workspace picker lists folders only and returns bounded, read-only directory metadata.
- Remote file preview cannot write, delete, upload, execute, or open a path in an external application.
- Codex Remote / Agent ACP is optional, can be disabled, and follows the same encrypted Host permission boundary as the rest of Remote.
- Removing a device revokes its credentials, membership, and active Remote connections.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Do I need a public IP or port forwarding?**

No. The Host only opens outbound connections and never listens on a public port.

**Can the service read my conversations?**

No. The service relays ciphertext only. Routing, authorization, presence and rate limiting require control metadata such as account and device ownership, online status, connection times and `connectionId`; prompts, conversation content, tool input and output, workspace paths and file preview contents stay unreadable.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**Which machine can act as a Host?**

Any signed-in Harness instance with the Remote plugin installed can act as a Host, whether on Windows, macOS, Linux, or even DSH Go.

**Can several devices connect to one Host at the same time?**

There is currently no limit on concurrent client connections, with RPC calls and streams isolated per connection.

**Which Harness versions are supported?**

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：The current baseline is `dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1`; `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5` and `0.2.0` rc.2 / rc.1 remain compatible on the same official carrier. See the [compatibility guide](docs/compatibility.md).

Harness `0.1.1-rc.2` ApiProxy support has been removed from the Host plugin, its bundled Remote client, and Android. Use a Host with the official Typert Remote carrier; Hosts that only provide ApiProxy or lack capability discovery are rejected, with no fallback.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：CodeX/ACP keep their independent data planes, and Desktop projections use Typert in memory.

**Why does the Linux installer require root?**

It configures a systemd system service, so the Host, Agent tools and remote terminals run with root privileges. Only expose it to trusted accounts.

**Can I install the iOS app directly?**

It is in TestFlight beta today and not publicly released; see [issue #20](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote/issues/20).

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：**How is this different from frp, a tunnel, or remote desktop?**

Conventional server-based TCP port forwarding routes traffic through a Server, making its bandwidth a potential bottleneck.

This project probes four connection modes in sequence to establish P2P connections even in complex network environments.

Remote desktop captures the entire computer screen and reproduces it on the client, placing demands on upload and download bandwidth as well as computer performance.

ds-harness-remote README · FAQ：This project encrypts and transmits only the messages needed by the native Harness conversation interface. General tool RPC and desktop control are not exposed, and permissions and approvals remain on the Host.

Tailscale, CF Turn, and UU Remote are also excellent solutions; choose whichever fits your needs.

ds-harness-remote README · Intelligent UI：[Intelligent UI](https://github.com/dreamfarer-space/deepseek-harness-intelligent-ui) lets models answer with cards, tables, charts, and forms. The Android client renders them natively and lists the plugin under **Plugins → Remote ready**, where you can enable or disable it and edit live settings.
